questions.q: What appears the first time you select the Python visual icon in a report?
options: An 'Enable script visuals' dialog, a one-time per-file prompt
A permanent error that blocks Python visuals entirely
A request to enter a license key
Nothing — Python visuals require no confirmation at all
questions.explain: This is a one-time, per-file security prompt — after selecting Enable, it doesn't reappear for subsequent Python visuals in that same file.

questions.q: How is the 'dataset' variable generated in a Python visual, compared to writing it manually?
options: Power BI auto-generates it from whatever fields you've dragged into the Values section — you never write the code that builds it
You must manually write pandas.read_csv() to create it
It's identical to the DataFrame from Lesson 8's Get Data script
Dataset must be typed in manually as a Python dictionary first
questions.explain: Just like Lesson 18's Run Python Script, the dataset DataFrame for a Python visual is auto-generated from the fields added to Values — the same underlying pattern, applied to a visual instead of a transform step.

questions.q: What does plt.show() do, and why is forgetting it a common mistake?
options: It's the line that actually tells Matplotlib to render the chart — without it, a script produces no visual at all
It saves the chart to a file on disk
It's optional and has no effect on whether the chart displays
It only affects chart color, not whether it renders
questions.explain: Without plt.show(), the plotting commands run but nothing actually gets rendered onto the Power BI canvas — an easy omission for anyone new to Matplotlib.

questions.q: What is one real limitation of Python visuals in Power BI?
options: Data is capped at 150,000 rows and 250 MB, all visuals render at 72 DPI, and they aren't interactive for cross-filtering other visuals
Python visuals support unlimited rows with no size restrictions
Python visuals can be used to cross-filter other visuals by clicking into them
Python visuals require no license of any kind, ever
questions.explain: These are genuine, documented limitations: a row/size cap, fixed 72 DPI resolution, and one-way interactivity (they respond to other visuals' filters but can't drive cross-filtering themselves).

questions.q: What license does viewing/refreshing/filtering a Python visual require in the Power BI service?
options: Pro or Premium Per User (PPU) — though authoring one in Desktop works for everyone
No license is ever required, in Desktop or the service
Only a Fabric Free license, nothing higher
A special 'Python Visual' add-on license separate from Pro or PPU
questions.explain: Python visuals require Pro or PPU to render, refresh, and filter properly once published to the service — a licensing consideration distinct from simply authoring one in Desktop.
